angle: Disney is known for its films, but its own results say most of its profit comes from somewhere else: in the nine months to June 2026, the Experiences division (parks, resorts, cruises, merchandise) made 61% of Disney's segment operating income, on less revenue than the entertainment division, because it keeps about 30 cents per dollar of sales against 12.
paragraphs: Disney is famous for its movies. But that's not where most of its profit comes from.
From October to June, Disney's businesses made {fourteen point eight billion dollars|$14.8 billion} in operating income.
{Sixty-one percent|61%} of it came from one division: Experiences. Theme parks, resorts, cruises and merchandise.
Movies, TV and Disney Plus? Just {twenty-eight percent|28%}. Sports, mostly ESPN, made the rest.
Yet entertainment brings in more revenue: {thirty-four point seven billion dollars|$34.7 billion}, against {twenty-nine point five billion|$29.5 billion} for Experiences.
The difference is margin. On every dollar of sales, Experiences kept about {thirty cents|30¢}. Entertainment kept {twelve|12¢}.
Last quarter, attendance at its US parks rose {three percent|3%}, and each guest spent {four percent|4%} more.
Disney makes the movies. The parks make the money. More on the channel.
